reviews.title: Entire Home doesn't mean privacy
reviews.text:
I booked an "Entire Home" with a "private backyard” from a Superhost. We arrived to two big dogs barking and a baby crying inside a trailer in the backyard, and the host's cars coming and going from the backyard. Their food was in the house's fridge, and their laundry and dishes in the machines. The listing only said they might be "on the property tending to the farm."

I paid a pet fee for my dog and had no idea other dogs would be there. The security camera was listed at the front door. It was on the back door, facing the "private" backyard.

I reported both issues to Airbnb. They found no policy violation on the camera, so the listing still shows the wrong location. They said the trailer was mentioned in an earlier version of the listing, but that text was later removed. I asked for the version from when I booked, and they couldn't provide it. They also couldn't explain why a host can stay on site now without saying so in the listing.

On another stay, an "Entire Home" turned out to be half of a duplex, with the Superhost living next door. The listing never said duplex.

Before you book, ask the host: "Will anyone else be living on the lot or next door, like in a guest house, trailer, or other unit?" 

Even with Superhosts, don’t assume "Entire Home" means privacy.

As a host, I am increasingly frustrated with Airbnb’s continued overreach into how property owners manage their own businesses. Their latest policies are yet another example of a company imposing unreasonable restrictions without adequately considering the impact on hosts.

Prohibiting hosts from asking guests to perform even basic, reasonable tasks, such as starting the dishwasher or disposing of trash in designated areas, is excessive. These are not unreasonable cleaning demands; they are common courtesies that help maintain properties and support efficient turnovers.

Airbnb seems to forget that hosts are the ones investing in, maintaining, and assuming the financial risks associated with these properties. Rather than treating hosts as valued business partners, Airbnb continues to dictate increasingly restrictive rules while collecting substantial fees.

There needs to be a reasonable balance between protecting guests and respecting property owners’ rights to operate their businesses. Airbnb has crossed that line.

Without hosts, Airbnb doesn’t have a business. It’s time they started treating us like partners instead of employees.

The real concern is Airbnb’s new restrictions on fundamental tools property owners use to protect themselves and establish accountability.

As a host, I feel extremely disappointed and pressured by Airbnb’s handling of my booking.

I clearly listed my property with no cancellation, yet I was repeatedly contacted by different Airbnb representatives pushing me to “change dates,” which in reality meant canceling or modifying the booking against my will.

This was framed as “not a cancellation,” but the outcome was the same: financial and calendar risk shifted entirely onto the host. I received multiple calls, repeated explanations, and changing language from support staff, which felt like pressure rather than support.

I understand and respect guest protection, but hosts also deserve clear rules, consistency, and protection when they follow the platform’s own policies. In this situation, I felt worn down rather than supported.

Airbnb should stop using indirect wording and repeated contact to push hosts into decisions they did not agree to. Transparency and respect for host policies are essential if this platform wants long-term trust from hosts.

reviews.title: Fraudulent representation
reviews.text: I have recently had a stay in a property that would not allow toilet paper to be used. The sewer backed up multiple times in a property managed by Host Elana in Tampa Florida. This is an investment company that manages several properties in the Florida area. After leaving the property early due to plumbing that would not function we left an honest review of the stay. The host responded in a retaliatory manor and charged us for the plumber to clear the plumbing system. After attempting to involve Airbnb with this we were stunned to discover that there are no options to speak with a manager, or any representative that can speak and understand the English language. After providing adequate documentation and photos of the filthy property and the hosts misleading advertisements Airbnb notified us that they are removing our review in spite of many other reviews siting the plumbing problems also. While looking at the reviews that are positive on all this management companies properties we discovered that they are all from manufactured accounts showing the guests leaving reviews all over the world in the same timeframe. In the future we will be contacting all hosts directly to book outside of Airbnb for a cheaper rate and more profit going to real people that are honest in business and who care about their homes and the people staying in them.

reviews.title: Worst customer service ever
reviews.text:
We are a Superhost and Guest Favorite property with nearly perfect five-star reviews, and we work extremely hard to maintain those standards. Unfortunately, Airbnb’s customer support has been the worst experience we’ve had as hosts.

Every time we faced a real issue with a guest, Airbnb did not take action. The support team dismissed serious concerns and showed no interest in protecting the host, even when we followed every rule and provided full evidence. It is clear that Airbnb is more focused on keeping bookings and collecting money than supporting the hosts who make this platform possible.

We deliver exceptional quality to our guests—and we expect basic professionalism and responsibility from Airbnb. Right now, the support system is broken, unresponsive, and leaves hosts completely alone when problems arise.

Airbnb needs to take host issues seriously and stop prioritizing profit over fairness.

reviews.title: Refund not received
reviews.text:
Do not use this platform!!! 
Dear all at airbnb ! I have been waiting for my deposit for the last 40 days . I have contacted all your support team and no one has answers to how and when my refund to my Apple Pay will be deposited . Everyday for 40 days I contact support and they keep making large excuses that it’s with the technical engineer team 
The host has given permission for the refund and I keep getting the run around

If I could give 0 stars, I absolutely would. The host cancelled our booking less than an hour before our flight, even though we booked the property a month in advance. We were already at the airport with elderly family members when the cancellation suddenly came through.

The “alternative options” they offered were completely unsuitable and far from the area we originally chose. The timing and handling of this situation were unbelievably irresponsible.

This entire experience caused us extreme stress and unnecessary trouble right before travelling. Absolutely unacceptable, and no guest should ever have to go through this.

reviews.title: Don’t force split stays
reviews.text:
I check back in occasionally to see if they’ve fixed the following…. Sadly not.  Back to booking dot com for me.


If I’m staying somewhere for a few nights don’t force on me a whole lot of stays where I’m required to change apartments.  If you want this feature make it a filter you can turn on and off. Defaulting to experiences when you open the app is also a nuisance.  

I remember when Airbnb was great.  That was some time ago.
